Only the linear part of the simplex normalization is applied to the summands. Thus weighted sums commute for arbitrary nonnegative coefficients, not merely weights summing to one, and all volumes acquire the same determinant factor.

In the standard simplex frame each r_i is positive by interiority. Coordinate minima and the maximum of the coordinate sum optimize separately over each summand, so the offset sums yield exactly the supporting simplex R, and R=S in the supporting case.

Checked the Minkowski volume polynomial and monotonicity of each mixed-volume argument in van Handel and Wang §1.1, https://arxiv.org/html/2507.20082v1#S1.SS1. Coefficient grouping gives the multinomial coefficient, and every mixed defect is nonnegative since A_i⊆P_i. Keeping the pure terms gives the desired weighted bound, including zero weights and dimension one.

In the zero-defect simplex case every positive-weight summand has equal volume to its enclosing P_i. Strict separation of an additional point and a cone to an interior ball give strict volume increase under proper inclusion, so equality forces A_i=P_i. In the containing-body case h_K≤h_S gives R⊆S and preserves both stated slack terms.

issues.defect: Q is introduced only by K⊆Q⊆S while the statement uses its Lebesgue volume and the proof invokes actual facet contacts for its minimum enclosure. The inclusions alone do not make Q measurable, closed or convex. For example Q=int T contains any sufficiently small full-dimensional K in int T, and T is its minimum enclosure, but Q has no points on its facets. The cited minimum-enclosure result is for compact convex bodies.
